title: 0.1.9's CI is red on Ubuntu: 0155's dying-worker arm depends on the runner's xargs, and 0158's gate_exec arm requires expect for a half that runs script
body:
## Problem

0.1.9's release push went red on CI's Ubuntu leg: run 37578519788, main at d7f2ed13, 2 of 2205 not ok, arms 309 and 1086. The tag's own run, 37578525064, is the same on Ubuntu, the same two arms, and green on macOS and Shell Script Analysis. Both arms are 0.1.9's, both depend on the runner, and in both the shipped runtime fails closed.

1. **contract.bats:1107, 0155's "a lint worker that dies".** It expects `lint: 2 file(s), 1 breach(es)` and the runner gives 2: "xargs: sh: terminated by signal 9", the parallel run exits 125, and lib/clean, which nothing is wrong with, has no verdict either. `gate_lint` (bin/.devbin/cmd/.lib/shell-gate:142) runs shellcheck directly in the `sh -c` worker xargs starts, and the arm's fake shellcheck kills that worker. GNU xargs 4.9.0 then exits without waiting for the workers still running, so the gate reads back before lib/clean's worker has written its status, and removes the scratch under it: the run ends with that worker's own error, "cannot create .../1.rc: Directory nonexistent", printed after the gate had finished. On macOS, BSD xargs and GNU xargs 4.11.0 both wait for the other workers, so the arm passed there, 3 of 3 under each and with the timing forced. The verdict was right everywhere (a dying worker fails the gate), but which other files keep their verdicts, and whether a worker outlives the gate's cleanup, depends on the runner's xargs.
2. **helpers.bats:2037, 0158's gate_exec arm.** `require_command expect` fails under CI because the runner has no expect. The arm's pty half runs `run_tty_eof`, which runs `script`, not expect (tests/lib/test_helper.bash:968; only `run_tty_answer` uses expect), so the arm requires a tool it never uses, and on Ubuntu the pty half has never run.

## Measured

An ubuntu:24.04 container mirroring the CI job (bats 1.12.0 from its tarball, the job's apt packages, the pinned shellcheck 0.11.0, CI=true, a non-root runner with sudo; /bin/sh is dash, GNU xargs 4.9.0, util-linux script 2.39.3, no expect, 8 CPUs) reproduces both, the first 3 of 3, each with the output the runner gave. Logs: ~/Devel/scratch/devbin-dc/ci019/runs/.

## Fix

1. `gate_lint` sends xargs's output through `cat >/dev/null`, which ends only once every process holding that pipe has exited. Each worker sh holds it as its stdout until it has written its status and exited, whether xargs waited for it or not, so the gate reads the statuses back, and removes its scratch, only after every worker has finished, on any xargs. A file whose worker dies has no verdict, a breach; every file whose worker was running keeps its own; nothing writes after the gate; and xargs's status still reaches the gate's warning through pipefail. The worker program is the released one. The 0155 arm keeps its lever, a fake shellcheck that kills the worker, keeps lib/clean's check going past the death, and asserts xargs's own report of the death, so a lever that misses the worker turns it red. A second arm kills xargs itself, which is what GNU 4.9.0's early exit amounts to, on every platform, so a gate that stops waiting when xargs does goes red on macOS as well as on Ubuntu. Both arms rest on the two checks overlapping, so they run the gate at two jobs whatever the host's CPUs, and lib/clean's check waits for lib/dies's lever to fire and leaves a file the arms fail on if it never does.
2. The arm guards its pty half with `require_pty`, as every `run_tty_eof` arm does, where it required expect. Its pty half then runs on Ubuntu for the first time, under util-linux script.

A subshell around each check, the first build, was set aside: it only moved the arm's lever from the worker to the subshell, and a worker killed outright still stopped xargs while its subshell could write after xargs had returned (critic-shell).

## Done when

1. The 0155 arm is red on d7f2ed13 in the container, and the new arm is red on d7f2ed13 in the container and on macOS under BSD and GNU tools. Both are green with the fix, in the container and on macOS. d7f2ed13's gate is the fix without the cat, so this is also the mutant that drops it.
2. Mutants each turn their arm red, on macOS under BSD and GNU tools and in the container: a subshell put back between the worker and shellcheck (the 0155 arm, at xargs's report of the death); pipefail off in gate_lint (both arms, at the gate's warning that the parallel run exited non-zero); a worker program that redirects its own stdout (the new arm); and the arms' own premise broken, one job where they need two, with and without a gate that prints a passing file's output (both arms, at their check of the overlap).
3. Before expect's requirement is replaced, the 0158 arm's pty half is shown to run under util-linux script in the container and to fail when it should: a mutant that breaks gate_exec's terminal flag turns it red there.
4. The next push's Ubuntu leg is green.

## Resolution

Landed at b6a39287 on a green full suite (vc's, 2210 of 2210 ok, 0 not ok, .errors empty, seal 20261007-0923). Done when 4 holds: hv pushed main at 7d1a3f4c, and the Ubuntu leg of its run, 37626021387, is green, 2220 of 2220 ok and 0 not ok. The 0155 arm (309) and the new arm (310) are ok, and the 0158 arm (now 1097) is ok with no skip, so its pty half ran under util-linux script on the runner.

1. `gate_lint` sends xargs's output through `cat >/dev/null`, which ends only once every process holding that pipe has exited. Each worker sh holds it until it has written its status and exited, whether xargs waited for it or not: at fd 1, or, under dash, as the copy dash saves while it runs the redirected shellcheck, which shellcheck does not inherit. Every path in the scratch is created by a process holding the pipe. So the gate reads the statuses back, and removes its scratch, only after every worker has finished, on any xargs: a file whose worker dies has no verdict, a breach; every file whose worker was running keeps its own; nothing writes after the gate; and xargs's status still reaches the gate's warning, through the pipefail set at the top of shell-gate. cat's own output goes to /dev/null, so it cannot fail before end of file and take xrc's status; nothing is written to the pipe, since each check writes to its own files. The worker program is the released one; against d7f2ed13 the code change is ` | cat >/dev/null` and the comment above it. GNU xargs 4.9.0, the Ubuntu runner's, exits at a worker killed by a signal without waiting for the workers still running. Measured in the container with cc's probe: rc 125 after 0.002 s, beside a worker still sleeping 2 s, whose file appeared 2.5 s later. That is how lib/clean lost its verdict on CI, and how its worker wrote into the scratch after the gate had removed it.
2. contract.bats's dying-worker arm keeps its lever, a fake shellcheck that kills the worker xargs started, and keeps lib/clean's check going past the death. It asserts 1 breach, lib/clean's verdict, xargs's own report of the death (BSD's "terminated with signal 9", GNU's "terminated by signal 9"), the gate's warning that the parallel run exited non-zero, and no status written into a scratch already gone. Its lever cannot drift off the worker unseen: a subshell put back between the worker and shellcheck turns it red at xargs's report.
3. A new arm kills xargs itself, which is what GNU 4.9.0's early exit amounts to, on every platform. It asserts the gate's warning that the parallel run exited 137 (the lever reached xargs), lib/clean's verdict (the gate waited), lib/dies's verdict (the lever took xargs and nothing else), 1 breach, and nothing written after the gate. So a gate that stops waiting when xargs does goes red on macOS as well as on Ubuntu, and so does one whose workers stop holding the pipe. It requires ps, which finds xargs.
4. Both lint arms rest on the two checks overlapping, so their helper makes the overlap and checks it: a fake nproc runs the gate at two jobs whatever the host's CPUs, and lib/clean's check waits for lib/dies's lever to fire, then a second more. If the lever never fired, the check leaves a file the helper fails on, whatever the gate prints of a passing file's output, and a line in that output saying why.
5. helpers.bats's gate_exec arm guards its pty half with `require_pty`, as every `run_tty_eof` arm does (cc's correction), where it required expect, which only `run_tty_answer` runs and the Ubuntu runner does not carry.

The first build ran each check in a subshell of the worker. critic-shell found that it only moved the arm's lever from the worker to the subshell: no arm killed a worker any more, a worker killed outright still stopped xargs, and its orphaned subshell could write after xargs had returned, on every xargs. The pipe is the critic's alternative, and vc's choice at review. critic-shell on the pipe found both arms blind on a host with one CPU, where the two checks never overlap, and cat able to end the wait if it failed; the helper now makes and checks the overlap, and cat writes to /dev/null. critic-shell on that found the overlap check leaning on the gate printing a passing file's output; it now fails on a file the fake leaves.

Evidence, in ~/Devel/scratch/devbin-dc/ci019/runs/, at 0cf6d4ba, the patch's commit in the scratch clone (ubuntu-final-20261007-081125.log, final-mac-{bsd,gnu}-20261007-080840.log, targeted-final-{bsd,gnu}-20261007-081126.log):

- Red on d7f2ed13, which is the fix without the cat. In an ubuntu:24.04 container that mirrors the CI job (bats 1.12.0, the job's apt packages and procps, the pinned shellcheck, CI=true, a non-root runner; dash as /bin/sh, GNU xargs 4.9.0, util-linux script 2.39.3, no expect), both lint arms are red 3 of 3, lib/clean with no verdict. On macOS the new arm is red 3 of 3 under BSD xargs and under GNU 4.11.0, lib/clean with no verdict; the 0155 arm passes there, since both wait.
- Green with the fix: all three arms 3 of 3 on macOS under BSD and GNU tools, and in the container.
- Mutants, each applied once, parsed, and red at its aimed assertion on macOS under BSD and GNU and 3 of 3 in the container: a subshell put back between the worker and shellcheck (the 0155 arm at xargs's report of the death, and the new arm at its 137, its lever then reaching the worker); pipefail off in gate_lint (both lint arms, at the gate's warning); a worker program that redirects its own stdout with exec (the new arm: lib/clean has no verdict); the arms' fake nproc at 1 (both arms, at the helper's check of the overlap), and the same with a gate that prints no file's output (both arms, at the same check). stdin_tty_flag never seeing a terminal turns the 0158 arm red at its pty assertion under BSD script and under util-linux script 2.39.3, so the pty half runs on Ubuntu now, and fails when it should.
- The targeted run (contract, helpers, neutral, documentation, readonlygit, harness and help): 268 of 268 under BSD tools and 268 of 268 with GNU tools first on PATH, the tree clean before and after; the only skips are require_command's own two.
- The lint gate over the tree is clean, 48 file(s), 0 breach(es): in the targeted run's lint arm under both tool sets, and in the container pinned to two CPUs, where contract.bats and helpers.bats whole are 144 ok, none failed, 3 of them skipped for that environment (no bash below 5, no en_US locale). In the container, a child dash runs under a redirection inherits no copy of the worker's stdout, as on macOS under dash, bash 3.2 and bash 5.3.
- critic-shell reviewed the first build (one critical, which is why the pipe replaced the subshell), the pipe (one warning, two recommendations and two style points) and the pipe with those folded in (no critical or warning; one recommendation and three style points). This patch folds in that last set as the critic gave it, and was not reviewed a fourth time.

Measured, and not this issue's: unpinned in the container, eight shellchecks at once in a 4 GiB VM, the kernel killed shellcheck 14 times (the VM's kernel log; 0.52 to 1.2 GB resident at the kill), and the gate counted each such file as a breach, d7f2ed13's gate and the first build's alike: dash wrote its "Killed" report into the file's output and the worker recorded 137. That fails closed. Pinned to two CPUs the gate over the tree is clean on both. It is not the container's alone: on macOS, shellcheck -x peaks at 2.07 GB on bin/devbin and at 1.0 to 1.3 GB on four of lib/cmd's handlers, so the eight largest at once would need 8.69 GB and the four largest 5.71 GB. gate_lint sizes its parallel run by CPUs, up to 8, and never by memory, so a machine with eight or more CPUs and less than that free, swap included, can have checks killed the same way. CI's Ubuntu runner ran the gate over the tree in contract.bats's lint arm on run 37578519788 without a kill.

Declared limits:

- A file xargs never started has no verdict, a breach, after a worker is killed by a signal: BSD xargs aborts, and GNU stops starting work (4.11.0 waits for the running ones; 4.9.0 exits, and the cat waits for them).
- A check whose worker is killed runs on as an orphan and writes only to the output file it already holds open, which the gate may already have removed; its file has no verdict, a breach.
- A worker that never exits, eg one whose shellcheck hangs, holds the gate. BSD xargs and GNU 4.11.0 already waited for every worker, so this is no new class there; it is new only on GNU 4.9.0 after a worker killed by a signal, where xargs no longer leaves the others behind.
- A gate killed outright leaves its scratch, and its workers finish into it. Nothing in devbin kills the gate.
- The lint arms see a gate that stops waiting only when it reads back within about a second of the lever, the time lib/clean's check still has to run; every run measured did, 3 of 3 on each platform.
